name: sar-logic-timing-gates-tie
description: Single-loop gate-level replay of the `tie` (input pinned exactly on the free-MSB decision threshold for the whole run -- the near-metastable case) loop of sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/ -- the SAME gate-level exact-tie-handling and sync-cadence-under-a-tie claim (README.md#target-specification, issue #11's synchronous-SAR timing-margin verification, DR-0008, spec/prior-art-survey.md Sec 4.3), against the SYNTHESIZED gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu7t5v0 netlist (design/sar-logic/flow/sar_ctrl/netlist/sar_ctrl.mcu7t5v0.synth.v, issue #272), split out of the original five-loop deck by issue #311 -- see sim/sar-logic-timing-gates-ok/testbench/tb.json's evidence notes for the full decomposition rationale (identical for every one of the five split experiments) and sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/ for the still-committed, unmodified five-loop deck kept for the nominal-PVT cross-check.
claim: spec/prior-art-survey.md Sec 4.3's sync-vs-async row ('a stalled decision corrupts one bit' vs 'a stalled decision stalls the whole conversion'), re-checked on the real synthesized gate netlist under a near-metastable comparator input: the conversion must still COMPLETE on schedule (drdy exactly 16 clocks apart) even on a dead-tie decision, plus the exact-tie code-handling bound (tie_code_deviation).
netlist_provenance: schematic (gate-level, single-loop `tie`: klt-synthesized gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu7t5v0 netlist wrapping sar_ctrl.v, issue #272 -- not yet placed-and-routed; DR-0023 follow-ons (b)/(c) own P&R/STA; split from the five-loop sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/ deck by issue #311's per-loop decomposition)
analyses: meas tran dev_tie MAX v(tie_dev) FROM=1.5u
meas tran tie_a WHEN v(tie_drdy)=1.4 RISE=2
meas tran tie_b WHEN v(tie_drdy)=1.4 RISE=7

tie_code_deviation.description: EXACT-TIE HANDLING -- UNCHANGED bound, carried over from the five-loop sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/ deck (issue #311). The code must land on one of the two adjacent codes (511 or 512) even on a real comparator-decision race, implemented by the same behavioural comparator model driving real gf180mcu sequencer logic. DR-0031 part 2 (issue #327) CORRECTED THE INSTRUMENT, NOT THE BOUND. Two changes, both about WHEN the comparison looks: (1) the measurement window now starts at FROM=1.5u instead of FROM=0.1u, i.e. after the DISCARDED FIRST CONVERSION (measured: drdy #1 rises at 1.06305 us and its window closes ~1.1257 us; drdy #2 rises at 2.06305 us, so 1.5u falls cleanly between them), because sar_ctrl_a has no reset on eng[9:1]/q[9:0]/c[9:0] and conversion 1's code is an arbitrary function of the power-up flop state (DR-0031 part 1(b)); and (2) the comparison is gated on a SETTLED drdy -- held off 0.5 ns after each drdy rise -- so it can no longer decode the output register's own clk->Q window (measured 0.186-0.199 ns) as if it were a code. THE LIMIT IS UNCHANGED, and every conversion inside the window is still held to it exactly as before. This deck is the family's most exposed to the strobe half: `tie` sits ON the 511/512 boundary, so up to 8 of its 8 conversions are full ten-bit carries (sim/sar-logic-timing-gates-tie/investigations/20260921-issue-337-tie-code-deviation-decode-transient.md measured 512 reported at 12 of 26 carries and at 0 of 30 non-carry conversions, with every settled code on 511 or 512, i.e. inside this bound).

tie_conv_period_ns.description: THE CADENCE CLAIM UNDER THE TIE -- UNCHANGED bound. Even with the comparator deciding a dead tie every conversion, drdy must keep arriving exactly 16 clocks apart, now measured on real gf180mcu logic -- the concrete, gate-level form of the sync-vs-async row (spec/prior-art-survey.md Sec 4.3).

notes: ISSUE #311 PER-LOOP DECOMPOSITION: this experiment is one of five (`sar-logic-timing-gates-ok/-lt/-xl/-bad/-tie`) split out of the single five-loop sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/ deck. The measurement definitions, bounds and 8.5 us duration are UNCHANGED; only how many loops share one ngspice deck changed. Rationale, the cost measurement that motivated it, and the 'five slugs vs one deck-variant axis' decision are in sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/investigations/20260917-issue-303-five-loop-composition-cost.md and design/sar-logic/flow/gen_sar_ctrl_gates_tb.py's own module docstring ('Per-loop timing decomposition (issue #311)').

COMPUTATIONAL COST: this loop's comparator drives the DUT gate input directly (like `ok`'s), so issue #296's investigation identified `tie` as one of the two loops (with `ok`) whose zero-time comparator step actually triggered the original 'Timestep too small' abort in the five-loop deck -- meaning `tie` is plausibly one of the MORE expensive loops per simulated ns even in isolation, not just a beneficiary of the split. A run's own record states the actual measured per-point cost; it should not be assumed equal to `ok`'s measured ~132 core-s without checking.

DECISION CHATTER IS EXPECTED HERE, AND IT IS THE EXPERIMENT (issue #322, spec/decision-records/DR-0029-tie-loop-decision-chatter.md -- read it before quoting a cost figure for this deck, or before reading a mid-rail `cmp` as a defect). Because this loop's input is pinned EXACTLY on the threshold, its comparator differential sits at ~1e-7 V -- below the model's own resolution, by construction of the stimulus -- so the hard sign test reverses between accepted timepoints: 651 reversals and 124.183 ns of mid-rail dwell over the full 8.5 us at tt/27C/3.30V, against 2 reversals / 0.204 ns for the `ok` loop running the IDENTICAL comparator and `cmp_out_rc`. DR-0029 settles this as a recorded property of the model rather than a defect, leaving the stimulus, the comparator and every bound below UNCHANGED, after measuring and rejecting both candidate fixes (a sub-LSB input offset makes the chatter WORSE at the proposed 1 uV -- which is ngspice's own default vntol -- and only removes it at ~0.3 LSB, by which point the loop is no longer near-metastable; strobing the comparator would redefine the decision instant the lt/xl/bad `cmp_delay` brackets and DR-0010's bisected 50/52 ns boundary are measured from). Two consequences for a reader of this deck: `v(tie_cmpo)` mid-rail is NOT issue #296's rejected soft comparator returning (the decision on `v(tie_cmpd)` is hard and always at a rail -- `probe_cmp_convergence.py --probe` prints both side by side), and `tie_code_deviation` is a check that the code lands adjacent to mid-scale, not a bit-wise reproducible number.

COMPUTATIONAL COST, MEASURED (issue #322): the chatter above is the dominant part of this loop's cost premium. Over the manifest's own unmodified 8.5 us window at tt/27C/3.30V, suppressing it via `probe_cmp_convergence.py --tie-offset 1m` (a measurement knob that writes nothing) takes the deck from 9216 to 7183 accepted timepoints but from 209.07 to 76.71 core-s -- ~2.7x -- because a chattering timepoint also costs more Newton iterations than a quiet one. DR-0029 records that saving as the strongest argument against its own decision and declines it anyway; budget this deck at issue #311's measured 233.7 core-s per point via sim/run_corners.py, not at `ok`'s ~132.

The behavioural CDAC/comparator model, comparator output slew fix (issue #296, `cmp_out_rc`) and start-pulse seeding (design/sar-logic/rtl/README.md's 'Real hardware note') are all UNCHANGED from the five-loop deck -- only the loop composition changed.

What this record does NOT claim: no place-and-route, no STA/timing closure (DR-0023 follow-ons (b)/(c), issues #274/#275) -- this is a pre-layout gate-level netlist wrapped directly in SPICE, with no extracted parasitics and no real interconnect delay. It is also not evidence about real CDAC settling or comparator behaviour.

DR-0031 PART 2, MEASUREMENT CORRECTION (issue #327): the code-error measurement in this manifest changed WHEN it looks and nothing else. (a) Its window starts at FROM=1.5u rather than FROM=0.1u, so the discarded first conversion -- invalid after power-up because sar_ctrl_a's eng[9:1]/q[9:0]/c[9:0] have no reset and are cleared only by conversion 1's own endconv = ph[13] -- is no longer scored (DR-0031 part 1(b) ratifies 'assert start >= 1 clock, then discard exactly one conversion' as the power-up contract). 1.5u is between the measured close of drdy window #1 (~1.1257 us) and the rise of drdy #2 (2.06305 us). (b) The comparison is gated on a settled copy of drdy (design/sar-logic/gen_sar_logic.py's CODE_SETTLE_GUARD_NS = 0.5 ns, a buffered drdy through a two-element RC), so it no longer reads the output register during its own clk->Q transition. NO BOUND MOVED -- DR-0031 Alternative (b) records why widening the limit to admit the 512 LSB transient would destroy sim/sar-logic-timing-gates-bad/'s negative control instead of loosening it. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE EVIDENCE TREE: this deck's netlist sha256 changed, so every record taken before this change stays committed (append-only) but is evidence for the OLD instrument, not this one.
